skills.name: Local time, standard time and zones

note.text: Longitude affects local solar time because Earth rotates. Places farther east are ahead of places farther west in the ideal longitude calculation. Earth turns through 360 degrees in about 24 hours, so 15 degrees corresponds to 1 hour and 1 degree to 4 minutes. Standard time is an adopted common time for a region, rather than a different clock for every meridian. Real civil zones follow political decisions and may differ from ideal equal-width zones.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Longitude affects local solar time because Earth rotates. Places farther east are ahead of places farther west in the ideal longitude calculation. Earth turns through {360} degrees in about {24} hours, so {15} degrees corresponds to {1} hour and {1} degree to {4} minutes. Standard time is an adopted common time for a region, rather than a different clock for every meridian. Real civil zones follow political decisions and may differ from ideal equal-width zones.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: For an exercise, suppose local time at Greenwich is {720} minutes after midnight. At {15} degrees east the ideal local solar time is {780} minutes after midnight. The example illustrates rotation, not a statement that every country on that meridian uses the same current civil clock. Always distinguish a theoretical longitude exercise from a real journey timetable.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Calculate the longitude difference, convert degrees to minutes and choose the sign: east ahead, west behind. Check whether the resulting minutes lie outside the current day. When asked about a real standard zone, use the stated offset rather than silently replacing it with longitude.

key_words.meaning: time related to the Sun at a particular longitude
a common clock time adopted for a region
the sign convention that adds time toward greater eastern longitude
a simplified longitudinal band used in teaching time differences

examples: An ideal calculation gives different noon times at different meridians.

A theoretical point east of Greenwich reaches solar noon earlier.
